name: Fake output hashes and keys
summary: Counts outputs whose hash or key is data as data carrier bytes
catches: Data hidden in the hashes and keys of outputs. A real hash or x-only key looks random, so one byte value eight times in a program or a run of six identical bytes, past up to seven leading zero bytes, or a taproot key that is not on the curve marks it as data, along with its same-type, same-value siblings. P2WSH outputs at one value of 353 sat or less also count when they pay three or more different scripts in one transaction: file encoders pay every chunk the same dust amount, and below 354 sat, the smallest dust limit BOLT 2 allows a Lightning channel, a commitment has no P2WSH output but its 330-sat anchors, two at most. So do 105 or more P2WSH or P2SH outputs of 900 sat or less each to different scripts, at any values: the funding of a BPUB file, whose spend reveals each script as a multisig holding the file. A Lightning commitment reaches 105 only with more than 100 HTLCs that small open at once.
passes: Payments to every address type, including vanity addresses whose hash or key starts with up to seven zero bytes, batched payments and pool payouts. The all-zero burn hash used by Stacks block commits is exempt, and so is an output that pays the script of a coin the transaction spends, such as change back to a vanity address.

example.note: an ACME file, a run of P2WSH outputs at the 330 sat dust floor whose programs hold a compressed HTML file

name: Bare data envelopes
upstream: merged in Knots 29.4.3; the switch is Plumb's
summary: Counts a run of pushes ended by OP_DROP or OP_2DROP as data carrier bytes
catches: A run of data pushes dropped again with `OP_DROP` or `OP_2DROP`, the envelope shape inscriptions use when `OP_IF` is not available. The whole run counts as data, not only the last push.
passes: Scripts that drop the result of an opcode, such as `<n> OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY OP_DROP` in timelocks. Only pushes followed by a drop count.

example.note: an 87 KB JPEG inscription in an ord envelope ended by `OP_2DROP`

name: Fake multisig keys
upstream: merged in Knots 29.4.3; the switch is Plumb's

amended_by.upstream: merged in Knots 29.5.1; the switch is Plumb's
amended_by.note: A key in a witness script (P2WSH, P2SH-wrapped P2WSH or a tapscript leaf) counts as proven only if a signature in the spend verified against it, so a signature check that never runs or fails harmlessly, such as one behind `OP_DEPTH OP_0NOTEQUAL OP_NOTIF` or one given an empty signature, proves nothing. `-rejectfakemultisig=0` turns it off with the rest of the rule.

summary: Counts the keys of a multisig that no signature in the spend proves, beyond 10 per script, as data carrier bytes
catches: File chunks dressed as public keys: a 1-of-15 multisig where one key signs and the other 14 each carry 31 bytes of a file. Keys that no signature in the spend can prove, beyond ten per script, count as data. Covers P2WSH, P2SH and tapscript `multi_a`.
passes: Real multisig and vaults, which since the fork leave at most ten keys unsigned in a script (a 2-of-3 vault with timelocked recovery branches; a plain 2-of-3 leaves one), including federations spending 11-of-15.
cost: A Liquid federation spend through its 2-of-3 emergency branch leaves 16 keys unsigned and is refused. There has been one since the fork, `97f7d78b0b9ad4d47e150659c3091d905c3565fe7e6fd8977e4326b2b7af2270` at block 963410. Other nodes and miners still carry it.

example.note: a file in 475 inputs at 546 sat each, 474 of them a 1-of-15 multisig whose 14 unused keys are file chunks

name: Token messages
upstream: open, as part of `-rejecttokens`; the switch is Plumb's
summary: Refuses an OP_RETURN that holds a JSON token message or an Omni Layer message
catches: Token operations written into an `OP_RETURN` that the Runes, Counterparty and OLGA checks of `-rejecttokens` do not match. A JSON object whose `"p"` field names the protocol is the BRC-20 format, which ico-20, crc-20 and others copy: `{"p":"ico-20","op":"mint","tick":"LEAF"}`. Omni Layer messages begin with `omni`. Most JSON mints on this chain are 41 or 42 bytes, under even a 42-byte `-datacarriersize`. The check runs under `-rejecttokens`, so `-rejecttokens=0` turns it off too.
passes: Every other `OP_RETURN`: swap and bridge memos, Stacks block commits, Babylon staking, and random data that happens to start with `{`. The payload has to start as a JSON object with a top-level `"p"` member whose value is a string.

example.note: the first ico-20 mint since the fork, `{"p":"ico-20","op":"mint","tick":"LEAF"}` in a 42-byte `OP_RETURN`

name: Unverified witness items
summary: Counts the bytes of witness items no verified signature check used, past 42 per input, as data carrier bytes
catches: Data handed to a P2WSH, P2SH-P2WSH or tapscript spend as witness items that the script drops, or passes to a signature check that never runs. The padded fake-key reveals since block 981910 put 13 items of 64 bytes, dressed as signatures, behind `OP_SIZE 64 OP_EQUAL OP_NOTIF` and drop them; a tapscript at block 981837 drops 555 bytes with eight `OP_DROP`s. After the script check, an item counts unless a signature that verified, or the key it verified against, has the same bytes.
passes: Signatures and the keys they verified against, copies of those keys, and up to 42 bytes per input that no signature verified: a hash preimage or a key a script only hashes, with a selector beside it. Of the 289,276 transactions mined from the fork through block 982560 that plumb11 relays and that carry witness item bytes on a P2WSH, P2SH-P2WSH or tapscript input, it refuses only the block 981837 tapscript.

example.note: a tapscript leaf of eight `OP_DROP`s before one key, spent with 555 bytes of data in the items it drops
